stem: Altostrat wants to optimize Cloud Storage costs for its growing media volumes. Some documentaries stay popular for years, while most news clips are rarely played after a few weeks. The content team cannot predict which items will stay popular. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Autoclass on the media buckets, so that each object moves to a storage class that fits its access pattern.
Add a lifecycle rule that changes every object to Archive storage 30 days after upload.
Store all new media in Coldline storage and serve it through Cloud CDN to reduce reads from the bucket.
Use Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions) to move objects between storage classes each night by view count.

explanation: The deciding facts are that access patterns vary by item and that nobody can predict them. Autoclass moves objects that are not accessed to colder storage classes, and it moves accessed objects back to Standard storage. Google lists unknown or unpredictable access patterns as a reason to use Autoclass. It needs no custom code, which fits the cost-management priority.

whyWrong.B: A fixed age rule also moves the documentaries that stay popular. Archive storage has higher access costs and a 365-day minimum storage duration, so frequent reads of those items cost more.
whyWrong.C: Coldline storage suits data that you read at most once a quarter. Popular items would pay retrieval costs, and Cloud CDN does not change the storage class of the objects in the bucket.
whyWrong.D: The custom mover is code to build and operate. It also pays the retrieval and early deletion fees that Autoclass does not charge after enablement.

sources.evidence: The Autoclass feature automatically transitions objects in your bucket to appropriate storage classes based on each object's access pattern.

sources.title: Autoclass

sources.title: Storage classes

stem: Altostrat wants its media library to stay available for playback if a whole Google Cloud region fails. The application must not change object paths during a failover. Viewers are spread across the United States, and Altostrat does not need to choose the exact regions that hold copies. Cost management is a top priority. Which bucket configuration should you recommend?

options.text: A regional bucket with turbo replication enabled
A dual-region bucket with turbo replication enabled
A multi-region bucket in the US location
Two regional buckets that Storage Transfer Service keeps in sync, with failover logic in the application

explanation: Dual-region and multi-region buckets both fail over automatically on a regional failure, with no change to storage paths. The deciding facts are that Altostrat does not need to choose the regions and that cost management is a priority. Multi-region storage costs less than dual-region storage, and Google recommends multi-region locations for content serving with cross-geography access. Turbo replication is a premium feature for a short RPO, which the case does not require.

whyWrong.A: A regional bucket keeps its data in one region, so a regional outage affects it. Turbo replication is an option of dual-region buckets, not of regional buckets.
whyWrong.B: A dual-region bucket meets the availability need, but it has the highest storage price of the location types. Turbo replication adds a premium charge for an RPO target that Altostrat did not state.
whyWrong.D: Two buckets need a sync job and failover code, and the object path changes during a failover. This breaks a stated constraint and adds operational work.

sources.title: Bucket locations
sources.evidence: RTO(recovery time objective)=0: automated failover and failback on regional failure (no need to change storage paths)

sources.evidence: Higher storage price than regions, but lower than dual-regions

stem: Altostrat wants automated summarization for diverse media: podcasts, interviews, and documentaries. Each summary must reflect both what people say and what appears on screen. The team wants the fewest components to build and operate. Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: Transcribe each file with Speech-to-Text, then send the transcript to a text-only model for summarization.
Send each media file to a Gemini model on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) with a summarization prompt.
Run label detection with the Video Intelligence API, and fill a summary template in Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions).
Train a custom summarization model on Agent Platform with a labeled set of summaries written by Altostrat editors.

explanation: The deciding requirements are one summary from both the audio and the pictures, and the fewest components. Gemini models natively understand text, video, audio, and images, so one request can summarize a video file together with its audio. Google describes a chain of a speech-to-text model and a text model as the older pattern, which adds latency and lowers performance.

whyWrong.A: A transcript loses what appears on screen. The chain of two models also adds a component and extra round trips.
whyWrong.C: Label detection describes what the camera shows, not what people say. A template cannot turn labels into a concise summary of an interview.
whyWrong.D: A custom model needs labeled training data, training, and serving. Gemini already summarizes video with audio without any training.

stem: Altostrat wants to analyze its podcast audio to identify trends, such as which topics gain an audience. Engagement data is already in BigQuery, and the media files stay in Cloud Storage. Analysts work in SQL, and the media files must not be copied to another system. What should you do?

options.text: Run a Managed Service for Apache Spark (formerly Dataproc) job that calls a custom model on the media files.
Load each media file into a BYTES column of a BigQuery table and parse the content with SQL string functions.
Label each file with the Video Intelligence API from Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions), and save labels in Firestore.
Create BigQuery object tables over the media buckets, extract topics with AI.GENERATE, and join the results with engagement data.

explanation: The deciding constraints are SQL for the analysts, no copy of the media files, and a join with engagement data. Object tables are read-only tables over unstructured objects in Cloud Storage. You can run inference over them and join the results with structured data in BigQuery. AI.GENERATE analyzes structured or unstructured data from SQL.

whyWrong.A: This moves the analysis out of SQL, and it adds Spark jobs and a custom model to build and operate.
whyWrong.B: Loading the files into a table copies them, which the stem does not allow. SQL string functions also cannot interpret audio or video.
whyWrong.C: Labels in Firestore create a new data silo outside the warehouse. Label detection also describes pictures, so it misses the spoken topics.

stem: Altostrat plans to migrate its on-premises archival workflow to Google Cloud. The archive holds several hundred terabytes on NFS servers. A new Cloud Interconnect connection has enough bandwidth to meet the deadline. Archived items are read less than once a year. Altostrat wants a managed transfer with incremental copies and the lowest storage cost. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Order a Transfer Appliance and ship the archive to Google.
Use Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data, with transfer agents on servers that mount the NFS shares.
Write the archive to a bucket that has Autoclass enabled.
Run gcloud storage rsync from one on-premises server on a cron schedule.
Write the archive to a bucket whose default storage class is Archive storage.
Write the archive to a bucket whose default storage class is Coldline storage.

explanation: Two facts decide the answer. First, the network has enough bandwidth, and Altostrat wants a managed transfer with incremental copies. Google suggests Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data in this case, and it supports full or incremental copies at petabyte scale. Second, the access pattern is known: reads happen less than once a year. Archive storage is the best choice for that pattern.

whyWrong.A: Google suggests Transfer Appliance when the network does not have enough bandwidth to meet the deadline. Here the bandwidth is enough.
whyWrong.C: Google does not recommend Autoclass when the data clearly fits the use case of one storage class. The archive access pattern is known.
whyWrong.D: The gcloud storage command suits smaller, as-needed transfers. One server with cron gives no agent pool and no managed error reporting.
whyWrong.F: Coldline storage suits data that you read about once a quarter. For data kept only for archiving, Archive storage is more cost-effective.

sources.title: Migrate to Google Cloud: Transfer your large datasets
sources.evidence: Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data is designed for large-scale transfers (up to petabytes of data, billions of files). It supports full copies or incremental copies

sources.title: Storage classes
sources.evidence: Archive storage is the best choice for data that you plan to access less than once a year.

stem: Altostrat wants secure, high-performance hybrid cloud connectivity for data ingestion from its on-premises ingestion site. Media uploads need tens of Gbps, and the traffic must not cross the public internet. The security team requires encryption between the on-premises router and Google's edge routers. What should you recommend?

options.text: Dedicated Interconnect with MACsec for Cloud Interconnect enabled
HA VPN tunnels over the internet to a Cloud Router in the ingestion VPC network
Direct Peering, with TLS configured on each upload client
Dedicated Interconnect, with no encryption configured on the connection

explanation: Three stated needs decide the answer: high throughput, no public internet, and encryption between the on-premises router and Google's edge. Traffic on Cloud Interconnect does not traverse the public internet. MACsec for Cloud Interconnect encrypts the traffic on exactly that link, between the on-premises router and Google's edge routers.

whyWrong.B: HA VPN uses the public internet here, which the stem rules out. Google also positions Cloud VPN for lower bandwidth needs and Cloud Interconnect for higher throughput.
whyWrong.C: Google recommends Cloud Interconnect instead of Direct Peering, except in certain circumstances. TLS on each client also leaves encryption to every upload tool.
whyWrong.D: Dedicated Interconnect meets the throughput need, but the security team requires link encryption. You add MACsec, or IPsec with HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect, to encrypt this traffic.

sources.evidence: MACsec for Cloud Interconnect uses IEEE standard 802.1AE Media Access Control Security (MACsec) to encrypt traffic between your on-premises router and Google's edge routers.

sources.evidence: Traffic between your networks doesn't traverse the public internet.

stem: Altostrat wants scalable, performant Kubernetes environments both on-premises and in the cloud. On-premises, it wants to run its content ingestion containers directly on its existing physical servers, with no hypervisor layer. Operators want to manage the on-premises and cloud clusters together from Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Move the ingestion workloads to Google Cloud VMware Engine and manage them with vCenter.
Install Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal (formerly Anthos clusters on bare metal), and use one fleet.
Install Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for VMware (formerly part of Anthos) on new vSphere hosts, without a fleet.
Run upstream Kubernetes with kubeadm on the servers, and forward its logs to Cloud Logging.

explanation: The deciding needs are containers directly on the existing servers and one place to manage all clusters. Distributed Cloud for bare metal runs GKE clusters directly on your own servers, instead of on virtual machines. You manage these on-premises clusters in Google Cloud, together with regular GKE clusters, as part of a fleet.

whyWrong.A: VMware Engine runs the VMware platform in Google Cloud locations, not on Altostrat's own servers. It also adds the hypervisor layer that the stem rules out.
whyWrong.C: The VMware option adds a hypervisor layer, which the stem rules out. Clusters outside a fleet also lose the shared management view.
whyWrong.D: Altostrat would have to operate the Kubernetes distribution itself. Forwarding logs does not give one place to manage the clusters.

stem: Altostrat wants to modernize CI/CD for containerized deployments with a centralized management platform. Cloud Build already builds the container images. Each release must move through development, staging, and production in a defined order. Some production clusters run on-premises and are registered to a fleet. Which two services should you add? (Choose two.)

options.text: Artifact Registry, to store and scan the container images in one location
Cloud Scheduler, to run kubectl apply against each cluster every night
Cloud Storage buckets, to hold exported image tarballs for each environment
Cloud Deploy, with delivery pipelines that target the GKE clusters and the fleet memberships
A Jenkins server on Compute Engine, with one deployment job for each cluster

explanation: The deciding needs are one central platform and a defined promotion order across cloud and on-premises clusters. Artifact Registry is a single location for container images, and it can scan them for vulnerabilities. Cloud Deploy promotes each release through a defined sequence of targets. It deploys to on-premises clusters through Connect gateway by using their fleet membership.

whyWrong.B: A nightly script has no promotion order and no release history. It pushes the same change to every environment at the same time.
whyWrong.C: A bucket of tarballs is not a container registry, so the clusters cannot pull images from it directly.
whyWrong.E: A self-managed Jenkins server is one more system to patch and operate. That conflicts with the requirement to simplify infrastructure management.

stem: Altostrat runs self-managed Prometheus servers for its GKE and on-premises workloads, and alerts go out mainly by email. On-call engineers miss critical alerts at night. Altostrat wants to stop operating Prometheus storage but keep its PromQL alert rules and Grafana dashboards. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Increase the Prometheus retention period and add larger disks to the Prometheus servers.
Replace the Prometheus metrics with log-based metrics in Cloud Logging, and rewrite every alert.
Adopt Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus for the cloud and on-premises workloads.
Send all alerts to an SMS notification channel instead of email.
Route critical alerting policies to PagerDuty, and keep email or Pub/Sub as a redundant channel.

explanation: Managed Service for Prometheus removes the Prometheus storage that Altostrat operates today. It keeps PromQL-based alerts and Grafana dashboards, and its collectors also run on-premises. For the missed alerts, Google recommends several notification channel types. When you use PagerDuty, use email or Pub/Sub as the redundant channel.

whyWrong.A: More retention and larger disks keep Altostrat operating Prometheus storage, which it wants to stop. This change also does nothing for the missed alerts.
whyWrong.B: Rewriting every alert discards the PromQL rules that Altostrat wants to keep.
whyWrong.D: Google states that SMS is not a fully reliable channel and might not be available in some regions. SMS alone needs a backup channel.

sources.title: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus
sources.evidence: Managed Service for Prometheus collects metrics from Prometheus exporters and lets you query the data globally using PromQL, meaning that you can keep using any existing Grafana dashboards, PromQL-based alerts, and workflows.

stem: Altostrat wants to design AI-powered detection of harmful content for podcasts, interviews, and news video. Its policy covers spoken hate speech and on-screen violence, with exceptions for news reporting and satire. Moderators must see why the system flagged each item. Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: Run Video Intelligence API explicit content detection on every video, and block items above a likelihood threshold.
Transcribe the audio with Speech-to-Text, and call the Natural Language API moderateText method on each transcript.
Use Gemini on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), with the policy in the system instruction and reasoning in JSON output.
Put a Model Armor template in front of the media library, and screen each media file when it is uploaded.

explanation: Three details decide the answer: audio and video together, a custom policy with exceptions, and an explanation for moderators. Gemini analyzes text, images, video, and audio, and it can detect custom moderation policies that you define. Gemini can also explain its reasoning. For moderation, Google recommends temperature 0 and JSON output.

whyWrong.A: Explicit content detection looks for adult content. It evaluates frames and considers visual content only, so it misses spoken hate speech and cannot apply the satire exception.
whyWrong.B: Text moderation of a transcript sees only the words. It misses on-screen violence.
whyWrong.D: Model Armor screens the prompts and responses of LLM applications. It is not a moderation service for a media library.

stem: Altostrat wants natural language interaction with the platform and 24/7 user support. The customer support team, not developers, will build and change the agent. The agent must answer open questions with generative AI and also follow fixed steps for account tasks, such as a subscription change. Which tool should Altostrat use?

options.text: Agent Development Kit, with the agent deployed on Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine)
Dialogflow ES, with one intent for each account task
An Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) media app, with a search widget on the website
CX Agent Studio in Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience (formerly Customer Engagement Suite and Contact Center AI)

explanation: The deciding facts are a team of non-developers and a mix of generative answers and fixed steps. CX Agent Studio is a minimal-code conversational agent builder. It creates agents with both generative AI and deterministic functionality for proactive, personalized self-service.

whyWrong.A: Agent Development Kit is a code-based framework, so it needs developers. The stem says that the support team builds the agent.
whyWrong.B: Google lists Dialogflow ES under legacy conversational agents. It is not the tool to choose for a new generative agent.
whyWrong.C: A media app gives search and recommendations over content. It does not hold a support conversation or run account tasks.

stem: Altostrat is launching a support chatbot that uses a Gemini model. The security team expects users to try prompt injection and jailbreak attacks, and it wants to stop unsafe responses. The team wants one central policy that screens prompts and responses, managed outside the application code. What should you recommend?

options.text: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the Agent Platform API (formerly Vertex AI API)
Model Armor templates that screen the chatbot's prompts and responses
Cloud Armor preconfigured WAF rules on the chatbot's load balancer
A daily Sensitive Data Protection scan of the chatbot conversation logs

explanation: The deciding needs are screening of both prompts and responses, protection against prompt injection and jailbreaks, and a central policy. Model Armor screens LLM prompts and responses. Its templates hold the filters and thresholds, separate from the application code.

whyWrong.A: VPC Service Controls reduces data exfiltration risk at the API boundary. It does not inspect the content of prompts or responses.
whyWrong.C: Cloud Armor protects against attacks such as DDoS, cross-site scripting, and SQL injection. It does not decide whether a model response is unsafe.
whyWrong.D: A daily scan finds sensitive data after the conversation. It does not block a prompt injection or an unsafe response when it happens.

sources.evidence: Protect against prompt injection and jailbreak attacks, preventing malicious actors from manipulating AI systems to perform unintended actions.

sources.title: Model Armor overview

stem: Altostrat must ensure that its AI systems are auditable. Auditors want a record of which users and service accounts called the prediction endpoint of the recommendation model, and when. Admin Activity audit logs are already in Cloud Logging, but they show no prediction calls. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Data Access audit logs for the Agent Platform API (formerly Vertex AI API).
Enable VPC Flow Logs on the subnet that the clients of the endpoint use.
Create a Cloud Monitoring dashboard that shows the prediction request count of the endpoint.
Enable Model Monitoring (formerly Vertex AI Model Monitoring) on the endpoint, and export its alerts to BigQuery.

explanation: The auditors need to know who called the endpoint and when. Prediction calls read user-provided data, so Data Access audit logs record them. These logs are not written until you enable them explicitly, which is why the Admin Activity logs show no prediction calls.

whyWrong.B: Flow logs describe network traffic. They do not record which principal called the API.
whyWrong.C: A request count shows the volume of calls, not who made each call.
whyWrong.D: Model Monitoring tracks drift and alerts when deviations pass a threshold. It does not record who called the endpoint.

stem: Altostrat trains a custom tabular model on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) that predicts the virality of new videos. Editors use the score to plan promotion. Altostrat must ensure that AI decisions can be explained: for one video, editors and auditors must see which input features raised its score. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Model Monitoring (formerly Vertex AI Model Monitoring) on the endpoint to track feature drift over time.
Log a sample of prediction requests and responses to BigQuery for later review.
Compare the evaluation metrics of the model with those of an AutoML (formerly Vertex AI AutoML) model.
Compute SHAP values for each prediction with the open-source SHAP library, and show them with the score.

explanation: The requirement is an explanation of one prediction, feature by feature. Google deprecated Vertex Explainable AI on March 16, 2026, and it suggests open-source libraries such as SHAP or LIME instead. Shapley values assign credit to each feature for the outcome of one prediction.

whyWrong.A: Model Monitoring tracks drift over time and alerts on thresholds. It does not explain a single prediction.
whyWrong.B: Logs record what went into the model and what came out. They do not show why the model gave the score.
whyWrong.C: Evaluation metrics describe the quality of the whole model. They do not explain the score of one video.

stem: Altostrat wants personalized recommendations that increase how much content each viewer consumes. Today, a function in Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions) ranks items with hand-written rules, and user events are already collected. The team has little ML experience, and the executives name reliability and cost management as top priorities. Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: Train a custom two-tower recommendation model on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), and serve it on GPU endpoints.
Send each viewer's watch history to a Gemini model on every page view, and ask it for ten titles.
Create an Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) media recommendations app from the user events, optimized for conversion rate.
Add more hand-written rules to the Cloud Run function, and review the results every week.

explanation: The deciding facts are the goal (more content consumption), little ML experience, and the reliability and cost priorities. These point to a managed service instead of a custom build. Agent Search media recommendations use the uploaded user events to personalize results. The conversion-rate objective targets the consumption of content.

whyWrong.A: A custom model is a build decision. It needs ML skills, training pipelines, and GPU serving, which conflicts with the team's skills and the cost priority.
whyWrong.B: A model call on every page view adds cost and latency at scale. It also ignores the user events that Altostrat already collects.
whyWrong.D: More rules keep the current approach, which does not learn from user behavior.

stem: Cymbal Retail wants to improve product discoverability and drive sales conversion. Today, its web application finds products by querying the relational databases for product names and categories. Cymbal does not want to build, train, or tune its own ranking models. Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: Add full-text indexes to the MySQL product tables, and tune the relevance weights for each category.
Generate embeddings for all products, and build semantic search on Vector Search in Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI).
Adopt AI Commerce Search (formerly Vertex AI Search for commerce), import the catalog, and record real-time user events.
Fine-tune a Gemini model on the product catalog, and have it return matching product IDs for each query.

explanation: The deciding constraint is that Cymbal does not want to build or tune ranking models. AI Commerce Search is a fully managed platform, and Google handles model training, tuning, and infrastructure. Its search is optimized for product ranking, which increases click-through and conversions. It uses real-time user events to produce search results, so recording events is part of the setup.

whyWrong.A: Full-text indexes still depend on keyword matching, which is the current weakness. Cymbal would also tune the relevance weights by hand.
whyWrong.B: Vector Search can power semantic search, but Cymbal would then build and operate the ranking and personalization itself. This breaks the stated constraint.
whyWrong.D: A fine-tuned model is a custom build that Cymbal must retrain as the catalog changes. This breaks the constraint against building and tuning its own models.

sources.title: What is AI Commerce Search?
sources.evidence: AI Commerce Search is a fully managed platform accessible to users who aren't developers, such as ecommerce admins. Google Cloud automatically handles the technical complexities like data preprocessing, training and tuning machine learning models, load balancing, and infrastructure provisioning.

stem: Cymbal Retail's virtual shopping agent calls a Gemini model on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) for every customer turn. Traffic has a steady daily baseline and sharp peaks during flash sales. The agent must stay responsive as traffic grows, and Cymbal does not want to pay for reserved capacity that sits idle. Which consumption approach should you recommend?

options.text: Buy Provisioned Throughput sized for the largest flash-sale peak, and route all traffic to it.
Buy Provisioned Throughput for the baseline traffic, and let spillover traffic use Standard PayGo.
Use Standard PayGo for all traffic, and retry the requests that the service throttles.
Send customer turns to Gemini batch inference jobs, and return each answer when its job completes.

explanation: Two constraints decide this: steady responsiveness and no idle reserved capacity. Google recommends that you cover baseline traffic with Provisioned Throughput, which gives guaranteed reliability for the core of the traffic. By default, Standard PayGo handles the spillover traffic above the baseline. The reserved capacity stays well used, and flash-sale peaks still get served.

whyWrong.A: Capacity sized for the peak sits idle for most of the day. Google notes that Provisioned Throughput can cause underutilization when traffic has spikes.
whyWrong.C: Standard PayGo is flexible, but it cannot guarantee a quality of service. Retries also add latency to customer conversations.
whyWrong.D: Batch inference is asynchronous and is not designed for real-time applications. Customers cannot wait for a batch job to finish.

sources.title: Consumption options
sources.evidence: Cover baseline traffic with Provisioned Throughput. This improves utilization of your reserved capacity, making it economical while providing guaranteed reliability for the core of your traffic.

sources.title: Consumption options
sources.evidence: By default, traffic that exceeds your Provisioned Throughput baseline (called spillover traffic) is handled by Standard PayGo.

sources.title: Consumption options
sources.evidence: While Provisioned Throughput offers the highest reliability, it can cause underutilization if your traffic has spikes. Similarly, PayGo might offer the maximum flexibility but cannot guarantee a quality of service.

stem: Cymbal Retail wants to derive product attributes from supplier titles, descriptions, and images. Each attribute must align with the product category and use only the values in Cymbal's existing catalog structure. Invalid values cause manual rework today. What should you do?

options.text: Send the supplier data to Gemini with a response schema that lists the allowed values for each attribute.
Ask Gemini for free-form attribute text, and extract the values from the output with regular expressions.
Run Cloud Vision API label detection on the product images, and save the returned labels as attributes.
Run Natural Language API entity analysis on the descriptions, and map each entity to the closest attribute.

explanation: The deciding requirement is that attributes must use only the values in Cymbal's catalog structure. When a prompt includes a response schema, the Gemini response always follows that schema. A schema can restrict the model to user-defined labels, such as the allowed values for a category, instead of labels that the model produces.

whyWrong.B: Free-form output can contain values that are not in the catalog, such as synonyms. The parsing code then fails or passes invalid values, so the manual rework stays.

stem: EHR Healthcare must leave one colocation facility before its lease expires. That facility runs containerized customer-facing applications on Kubernetes. stem: EHR Healthcare must provide at least 99.9% availability for its customer-facing applications, which it is moving to GKE in one region. A single zone outage must not stop the applications or the cluster control plane. What should you do?

Create two zonal clusters in the same zone, and split the traffic between them.

stem: EHR Healthcare runs its customer-facing container applications on several GKE clusters for development, staging, and production. Many past outages came from misconfigured systems. Write a runbook for configuration changes, and review each change in a weekly meeting.
Enable Policy Controller on the fleets, and apply policy bundles that block noncompliant resources.
Copy the production configuration to the other clusters each night with a kubectl script.

Policy Controller enforces programmable policies as guardrails, so it blocks noncompliant changes.

stem: EHR Healthcare serves medical offices, hospitals, and insurance providers in many countries from GKE in one region. EHR wants to reduce latency to all customers and keep a single public IP address for its web applications. Responses contain patient data and must not be cached. What should you do?

options.text: Keep one region, and enable Cloud CDN on the load balancer for all responses.
Deploy regional external Application Load Balancers in several regions, and give each customer the closest address.
Keep one region, and move the cluster to machine types with more CPUs and memory.
Deploy the applications to clusters in several regions, behind one global external Application Load Balancer.

explanation: The deciding requirements are lower latency for users in many countries, one public IP address, and no caching of patient data. Google recommends the global external Application Load Balancer for globally dispersed users or backends in multiple regions. One anycast IP address fronts backends in regions around the world. Backends in several regions end connections close to users.

whyWrong.A: Cloud CDN caches responses, which the stem rules out for patient data. Uncached requests still travel to one distant region.
whyWrong.B: Each regional load balancer has its own address, so EHR loses the single IP address. Customers must also choose an address.
whyWrong.C: Larger machines do not shorten the network distance to customers in other countries.

sources.title: External Application Load Balancer overview
sources.evidence: Use this load balancer for external HTTP(S) workloads with globally dispersed users or backend services in multiple regions.

sources.title: Cloud Load Balancing overview
sources.evidence: With Cloud Load Balancing, a single anycast IP address is the frontend for all of your backend instances in regions around the world.

sources.title: Cloud Load Balancing overview
sources.evidence: You can distribute your backends in single or multiple regions to terminate connections close to your users and to meet your high availability requirements.

stem: EHR Healthcare wants to onboard new insurance providers as quickly as possible. Each provider needs secure access to EHR's claims and eligibility APIs, with documentation and self-service app registration. EHR also wants rate limits without changes to the backend services. What should you recommend?

options.text: Publish the APIs through Apigee API proxies, and give providers a developer portal for documentation and app registration.
Give each provider a service account key, and let the provider call the backend services directly.
Create a Cloud VPN tunnel for each provider, and send each provider the API documentation by email.
Expose each backend service on its own load balancer, and add rate-limit code to each service.

explanation: The deciding requirements are fast, self-service onboarding and rate limits without backend changes. Apigee gives providers a developer portal where they discover APIs, read documentation, and register apps. The Apigee proxy layer controls security, rate limiting, and quotas. Because the policies run in the proxy layer, the backend services stay unchanged.

whyWrong.B: Direct access gives no central place for rate limits, documentation, or self-service registration. Each new provider also needs manual setup.
whyWrong.C: A VPN tunnel for each provider adds network work to every onboarding. It also gives no documentation portal and no rate limits.
whyWrong.D: Rate-limit code in each service changes the backends, which the stem rules out. There is also no portal for self-service onboarding.

sources.title: What is Apigee?
sources.evidence: Apigee offers API producers a developer-focused portal where client app developers can discover your APIs, find the documentation required to build applications using them, and register as an app developer to stay in sync with any updates or changes.

sources.title: What is Apigee?
sources.evidence: The proxy layer gives you granular control over security, rate limiting, quotas, analytics, and more for all of your services.

sources.title: What is Apigee?
sources.evidence: Because the policies and actions are implemented on Apigee, in the API proxy layer, your underlying backend services can remain unchanged.

stem: EHR Healthcare needs interfaces to ingest and process data from new providers. The providers send clinical records as FHIR resources through EHR's APIs. Analysts need each change in BigQuery within minutes for trend reports, and EHR does not want to write custom ETL code. What should you do?

options.text: Store the records in a Cloud SQL for MySQL database, and export the database to BigQuery each night.
Write the records to a Cloud Healthcare API FHIR store, and configure BigQuery streaming on the store.
Write the records to Cloud Storage, and import them into a FHIR store that has BigQuery streaming enabled.
Publish the records to Pub/Sub, and write a Dataflow pipeline that parses FHIR and loads BigQuery.

explanation: The deciding requirements are changes in BigQuery within minutes and no custom ETL code. A FHIR store in the Cloud Healthcare API can export resources to BigQuery each time a resource is created, updated, patched, or deleted. This BigQuery streaming keeps the dataset in sync in near real time.

whyWrong.A: A nightly export does not meet the need for data within minutes. EHR would also have to map FHIR resources to tables itself.
whyWrong.C: Changes that you import from Cloud Storage are not streamed to BigQuery. Analysts would not see these records.
whyWrong.D: The pipeline works, but it is custom ETL code, which the stem rules out.

sources.title: Streaming FHIR resource changes to BigQuery
sources.evidence: This page explains how to configure a FHIR store to automatically export FHIR resources to BigQuery tables every time a FHIR resource is created, updated, patched, or deleted. This process is called BigQuery streaming.

sources.title: Streaming FHIR resource changes to BigQuery
sources.evidence: Synchronize the data in a FHIR store with a BigQuery dataset in near real time.

sources.title: Streaming FHIR resource changes to BigQuery

stem: EHR Healthcare wants to make predictions on industry trends, such as monthly claim volumes by region, from provider data in BigQuery. EHR's analysts know SQL but not Python or ML frameworks. EHR wants to avoid moving the data, and it does not want to create and manage a model. What should you do?

options.text: Export the data to Cloud Storage, and train a forecasting model with Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) custom training.
Create an `ARIMA_PLUS` model with BigQuery ML, and run `ML.FORECAST` against it on a schedule.
Use the `AI.FORECAST` function in BigQuery with the built-in TimesFM model.
Build Looker dashboards of historical volumes, and let analysts extend the trend lines by hand.

explanation: Three constraints decide this: SQL skills, no data movement, and no model to create or manage. BigQuery ML runs where the data is, so the data stays in the warehouse. The `AI.FORECAST` function uses the built-in TimesFM model, and it does not require you to create and manage a model.

whyWrong.A: Custom training needs a data export and ML programming skills that the analysts do not have.
whyWrong.B: `ARIMA_PLUS` runs in SQL, but it requires you to create and manage a model, which the stem rules out.
whyWrong.D: Dashboards show past data, but they do not produce predictions.

sources.title: Forecasting overview
sources.evidence: By using the AI.FORECAST function with the built-in TimesFM model. Use this approach when you need to forecast future values for a single variable or multiple variables. This approach doesn't require you to create and manage a model.

sources.title: Introduction to ML in BigQuery
sources.evidence: BigQuery ML increases the speed of model development and innovation by removing the need to move data from the data warehouse.

sources.title: Introduction to ML in BigQuery
sources.evidence: However, with BigQuery ML, SQL practitioners can use existing SQL tools and skills to build and evaluate models, and to generate results from LLMs and Cloud AI APIs.

stem: EHR Healthcare manages its users in Microsoft Active Directory. EHR wants employees to sign in to Google Cloud with their Active Directory credentials, and the Active Directory MFA policies must still apply. When a user is deleted in Active Directory, the deletion must also reach Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Identity account for each employee by hand, and ask each user to choose a new password.
Create a service account for each employee, and distribute the keys through Active Directory Group Policy.
Sync password hashes from Active Directory to Cloud Identity, and let Google check each password at sign-in.
Sync users and groups to Cloud Identity with Google Cloud Directory Sync, and use Active Directory for SAML single sign-on.

explanation: The deciding requirements are Active Directory credentials, Active Directory MFA, and automatic deletions. Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) periodically syncs users and groups from Active Directory to Cloud Identity, and it also propagates deletions. With SAML single sign-on, Google Cloud delegates authentication to Active Directory. Only Active Directory then manages credentials and enforces MFA.

whyWrong.A: Manual accounts create a second set of credentials. Deletions in Active Directory also do not reach Google Cloud.
whyWrong.B: Service accounts are identities for workloads, not for people. Distributed keys are also hard to control.
whyWrong.C: Google then checks the passwords, so Active Directory no longer controls the sign-in or its MFA policies.

sources.title: Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory
sources.evidence: Relevant users and groups are synchronized periodically from Active Directory to Cloud Identity or Google Workspace.

sources.title: Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory
sources.evidence: This delegation ensures that only Active Directory manages user credentials and that any applicable policies or multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms are being enforced.

sources.title: Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory
sources.evidence: Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) is a free Google-provided tool that implements the synchronization process.

stem: EHR Healthcare will store protected health information (PHI) for US customers in Google Cloud and must maintain HIPAA compliance. The compliance officer asks what EHR must do before it moves any PHI. What should you do first?

options.text: Request a HIPAA certification for Google Cloud from Google, and add it to the audit file.
Accept the Google Cloud Business Associate Agreement (BAA), and use only BAA-covered products for PHI.
Enable CMEK on all storage services, because CMEK makes the workloads HIPAA compliant.
Put PHI in Preview healthcare features, because Google manages their HIPAA controls.

explanation: The deciding requirement is HIPAA compliance before PHI moves. Google lists the execution of a Google Cloud BAA as an essential best practice. EHR must also not use products that the BAA does not cover when it works with PHI. HIPAA compliance is a shared responsibility, so EHR must still configure its environment correctly.

whyWrong.A: No certification recognized by the US HHS exists for HIPAA compliance. Compliance is a shared responsibility between EHR and Google.
whyWrong.C: CMEK is one control, but it does not make a workload compliant by itself. EHR still needs the BAA and covered products.
whyWrong.D: Google advises against Pre-GA offerings with PHI unless the terms say otherwise. Compliance also stays a shared responsibility.

sources.title: HIPAA Compliance on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Execute a Google Cloud BAA. You can follow the instructions in the Privacy compliance and records for Google Cloud to review and accept the BAA.

sources.title: HIPAA Compliance on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Disable or otherwise ensure that you do not use Google Cloud Products that are not explicitly covered by the BAA (see Covered Products) when working with PHI.

sources.title: HIPAA Compliance on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: It is important to note that there is no certification recognized by the US HHS for HIPAA compliance and that complying with HIPAA is a shared responsibility between the customer and Google.

stem: EHR Healthcare needs consistent logging, log retention, monitoring, and alerting across many projects. Today, teams use different open source tools, and email alerts are often ignored. Compliance requires EHR to keep application logs in one place for several years. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Route logs with an organization-level aggregated sink to a log bucket in a central project, with custom retention.
Keep the default log buckets, and ask each team to export its logs before the default retention ends.
Send every warning-level log entry to a shared email list, so that more people see each problem.
Run a separate open source monitoring stack in each project, and let each team choose its own alert rules.
Define SLOs for the customer-facing services, and alert on error budget burn rate through an on-call channel such as PagerDuty.

explanation: The deciding needs are logs in one place with long retention, and alerts that people act on. Aggregated sinks combine and route logs from the organization to a central location. A log bucket has a configurable retention period. Burn-rate alerts show how fast a service uses its error budget, so they point to problems that affect users.

whyWrong.B: Manual exports are inconsistent and easy to forget. The logs also stay spread across projects.
whyWrong.C: More email alerts add noise, which is why alerts are ignored today.
whyWrong.D: Separate stacks keep the inconsistent monitoring that the executive statement names as a cause of outages.

sources.title: Collate and route organization- and folder-level logs to supported destinations
sources.evidence: You can use aggregated sinks in Cloud Logging to combine and route logs from resources in your organization or folder to a centralized location.

sources.title: Configure log buckets
sources.evidence: Cloud Logging buckets to store and centralize your log data using the Google Cloud console, Google Cloud CLI, or the Logging API. You can also configure retention periods and lock buckets to meet compliance requirements.

sources.title: Alerting on your burn rate
sources.evidence: The burn rate tells you how fast you are consuming your error budget for a compliance period.

stem: EHR Healthcare wants more insight into healthcare trends from de-identified clinical notes that providers send. EHR needs medical concepts, such as medications and conditions, extracted into BigQuery columns for reports. EHR wants a prebuilt, generally available model, not a custom-trained one. EHR does not want to adopt a service that Google has deprecated. What should you do?

options.text: Send the notes to a GA Gemini model on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), and set a response schema.
Send the notes to the Healthcare Natural Language API, and load the extracted medical entities into BigQuery.
Send the notes to the Cloud Natural Language API for entity analysis, and load the general entities into BigQuery.
Load the raw notes into BigQuery, and count keyword matches for each medication and condition with SQL.

explanation: The deciding constraints are a prebuilt, generally available model and no deprecated services. Google deprecated the Healthcare Natural Language API, and it names a GA Gemini model on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) as the alternative. A response schema makes the Gemini output always follow the defined structure, so the results load into BigQuery columns.

whyWrong.B: The Feature deprecations page lists the Healthcare Natural Language API as deprecated on May 27, 2025. Its API page gives May 27, 2026 as the shutdown date. The stem rules out a deprecated service.
whyWrong.C: Entity analysis in the Cloud Natural Language API returns general entities. It does not target medical concepts such as medications and conditions.
whyWrong.D: Keyword counts miss synonyms, abbreviations, and negations in clinical text. The trend data would be unreliable.

sources.title: Feature deprecations
sources.evidence: The Healthcare Natural Language API is deprecated. As an alternative, you can use a Generally Available (GA) Gemini model on Vertex AI.

sources.title: Healthcare Natural Language API
sources.evidence: The Healthcare Natural Language API is deprecated and will be shut down on May 27, 2026.

sources.title: Structured output
sources.evidence: To specify the structure of a model's output, define a response schema, which works like a blueprint for model responses. When you submit a prompt and include the response schema, the model's response always follows your defined schema.

stem: EHR Healthcare wants continuous deployment so that it can update its software at a fast pace. Each release must move through test, staging, and production GKE clusters in order. In production, a new version must reach a small share of users first, so that a bad release does not affect all customers. What should you do?

options.text: Run kubectl apply from each developer's workstation against each cluster after the tests pass.
Use a Cloud Build trigger that replaces all production Pods with the new version in one step.
Create a new production cluster for each release, and switch DNS to it after a manual check.
Use a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline with a promotion sequence, and a canary strategy for the production target.

explanation: The deciding requirements are an ordered promotion through environments and a partial first release in production. Cloud Deploy delivers applications to a series of targets in a defined promotion sequence. A canary deployment sends the new version to a subset of users before the full rollout, so EHR can confirm that the version is reliable.

whyWrong.A: Manual deployments from workstations are inconsistent and have no promotion sequence. Misconfigured systems already caused many outages.
whyWrong.B: All users get the new version at once, so a bad release affects every customer.
whyWrong.C: A DNS switch moves all users at once. A new cluster for each release also adds cost and operational work.

sources.title: Overview of Cloud Deploy
sources.evidence: Cloud Deploy is a managed service that automates delivery of your applications to a series of target environments in a defined promotion sequence.

sources.title: Use a canary deployment strategy
sources.evidence: A canary deployment is a progressive rollout of an application that splits traffic between an already-deployed version and a new version, rolling it out to a subset of users before rolling out fully.

sources.title: Use a canary deployment strategy
sources.evidence: A canary deployment gives you a chance to partially release your application. In this way, you can ensure the new version of your application is reliable before you deliver it to all users.

stem: EHR Healthcare is adapting its disaster recovery plan. Its customer-facing applications run on a regional GKE cluster and use a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance with high availability in the same region. EHR wants to recover from a full regional outage with an RTO and RPO measured in minutes, not hours. What should you do?

options.text: Rely on the Cloud SQL high availability configuration, and keep automated daily backups.
Export the database to a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket each night, and import it in another region after an outage.
Create a cross-region read replica of the Cloud SQL instance, and keep a standby GKE cluster in a second region.
Back up with Backup for GKE and Cloud SQL backups, and restore both in another region after an outage.

explanation: The deciding requirement is recovery from a regional outage in minutes. A Cloud SQL HA instance is regional, so it becomes unavailable when its region fails. Google's DR design for Cloud SQL uses a cross-region read replica, because failover to another region is faster than recreating a database. A standby cluster in the second region lets the application tier fail over too.

whyWrong.A: An HA instance protects against a zone failure, but it is unavailable when its whole region fails. Daily backups also allow up to a day of data loss.
whyWrong.B: A nightly export allows up to a day of data loss. Export and import also take longer than a replica failover, especially for large databases.
whyWrong.D: Restore-based recovery takes longer than a replica failover, especially for large databases. The RTO would not be minutes.

sources.title: About disaster recovery (DR) in Cloud SQL
sources.evidence: Cloud SQL is a regional service (when Cloud SQL is configured for high availability (HA)). Therefore, if the Google Cloud region that hosts a Cloud SQL database becomes unavailable, then the Cloud SQL database also becomes unavailable.

sources.title: About disaster recovery (DR) in Cloud SQL
sources.evidence: The DR plan requires you to configure a cross-region read replica in Cloud SQL. A failover based on export/import or backup/restore is also possible, but that approach takes longer, especially for large databases.

sources.title: About disaster recovery (DR) in Cloud SQL
sources.evidence: The required recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) are in minutes rather than in hours. Failing over to another region is faster than recreating a database.

stem: EHR Healthcare wants to decrease infrastructure administration costs for its container platform after the migration. Its operations team spends much of its time on node upgrades, node scaling, and security settings for Kubernetes clusters. What should you do?

options.text: Run the applications on GKE Autopilot clusters, where Google manages the nodes, scaling, and security settings.
Run GKE Standard clusters, and write scripts that upgrade and resize the node pools each week.
Run self-managed Kubernetes on Compute Engine VMs in a managed instance group.
Keep the Kubernetes clusters in the remaining colocation facilities, and add more operators to the team.

explanation: The deciding requirement is lower administration cost for the clusters. In GKE Autopilot, Google manages the infrastructure configuration, including nodes, scaling, and security settings. Google also handles node creation, upgrades, and repairs, so the operations team no longer spends time on these tasks.

whyWrong.B: Custom scripts keep node management with EHR, and they add code to maintain.
whyWrong.C: Self-managed Kubernetes keeps all control plane and node work with EHR, which increases administration.
whyWrong.D: More operators increase costs. Google Cloud is also chosen to replace the colocation facilities.

sources.title: GKE Autopilot overview
sources.evidence: GKE Autopilot is a mode of operation in GKE in which Google manages your infrastructure configuration, including your nodes, scaling, security, and other preconfigured settings.

sources.title: GKE Autopilot overview
sources.evidence: Node management: Google manages worker nodes, so you don't need to create new nodes to accommodate your workloads or configure automatic upgrades and repairs.

stem: KnightMotives wants to monetize corporate data to finance new technology investments. An insurance partner wants to join KnightMotives driving data with its own policy data. After past data breaches, KnightMotives will not let the partner see or copy raw driver records. KnightMotives also wants to allow only the analyses that it approves. What should you recommend?

options.text: Export aggregated CSV files to Cloud Storage each week, and send the partner signed URLs to download them.
List the driving tables in a standard BigQuery sharing (formerly Analytics Hub) exchange, and let the partner subscribe.
Share the driving data through a BigQuery data clean room with analysis rules and approved query templates.
Grant the partner's analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role on the dataset that contains the driving tables.

explanation: The deciding needs are a join with partner data, no access to raw records, and only approved analyses. Data clean rooms let several parties join and analyze data without moving or revealing the underlying data. Analysis rules help prevent raw access and enforce query restrictions. Google also recommends query templates to restrict execution to approved queries.

whyWrong.A: The partner gets copies of the data, which it can keep and share. KnightMotives also cannot limit which analyses the partner runs on the files.
whyWrong.B: Standard BigQuery sharing exchanges share data at scale, but Google recommends data clean rooms for sensitive and protected data. Subscribers can read the shared records.
whyWrong.D: The Data Viewer role gives read access to the raw tables. It does not restrict the partner to approved analyses.

sources.title: Share sensitive data with data clean rooms
sources.evidence: You can use data clean rooms to establish a security-enhanced environment. In this environment, multiple parties share, join, and analyze their data assets. This collaboration occurs without moving or revealing the underlying data.

sources.title: Share sensitive data with data clean rooms
sources.evidence: As a data contributor, you configure analysis rules on the resources that you share in the data clean room. Analysis rules help prevent raw access to underlying data and enforce query restrictions.

sources.title: Share sensitive data with data clean rooms
sources.evidence: Analysis rules in data clean rooms provide privacy controls, but they might not fully prevent sophisticated queries from extracting unauthorized data. To maintain control and restrict execution to approved queries, use query templates.

stem: KnightMotives's online build-to-order system is unreliable. When the outdated ERP slows down, order submissions time out, and dealers lose orders. KnightMotives will replace the ERP gradually over several years. You need to make order intake reliable now without changing the ERP. What should you do?

options.text: Increase the request timeout on the web tier, and add browser retries for failed order submissions.
Publish orders to Pub/Sub, and have a pull subscriber write them to the ERP at a rate it can handle.
Replace the ERP with a new cloud-based ERP first, and then change the ordering website to use it.
Add more web server instances behind the load balancer, so that more order submissions run at once.

explanation: The deciding constraint is that the ERP stays slow for now. Pub/Sub decouples the services that produce messages from the services that process them. A pull subscriber requests messages when it is ready, so the ERP receives orders at a rate it can handle. Pub/Sub keeps delivering an unacknowledged message until its retention duration expires.

whyWrong.A: Longer timeouts and retries still wait on the slow ERP. Retries also add load to the ERP when it is already slow.
whyWrong.C: The ERP is replaced gradually over several years, so this fix comes too late. Order intake needs a fix now.
whyWrong.D: More web servers do not help, because the ERP is the bottleneck. More concurrent submissions can make the ERP slower.

sources.title: What is Pub/Sub?
sources.evidence: Pub/Sub is an asynchronous and scalable messaging service that decouples services producing messages from services processing those messages.

sources.title: Subscription overview
sources.evidence: Pull subscriptions use a subscriber client to request messages from the Pub/Sub server.

sources.title: Overview of the Pub/Sub service
sources.evidence: An unacknowledged message continues to be delivered until the message retention duration expires since the message was published.

stem: KnightMotives needs reliable data transmission from vehicles to support real-time AI features. Vehicles in rural areas lose connectivity, and then they send buffered telemetry in bursts when they reconnect. The platform must absorb the bursts without losing data. It must also serve low-latency reads of recent readings for each vehicle. Which two services should you use? (Choose two.)

options.text: Pub/Sub, to receive telemetry from the vehicles and decouple them from the processing services
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, to store every reading as a row in one relational table
Bigtable, to store one row per reading with a row key that includes the vehicle ID and timestamp
Filestore, to store one file for each vehicle for each day of readings
A self-managed message broker on one Compute Engine VM, to queue the telemetry

explanation: The deciding needs are burst absorption and low-latency reads for each vehicle. Pub/Sub gathers events from many clients at the same time, and it decouples producers from consumers. Bigtable supports high read and write throughput at low latency. The Bigtable time-series guide shows one row per event, with the timestamp as the row key suffix.

whyWrong.B: One relational instance must absorb every burst of writes. Bigtable is the documented fit for high-throughput time-series and IoT data.
whyWrong.D: File shares give no indexed, low-latency reads of recent readings for each vehicle. They also add no buffering for bursts.
whyWrong.E: One VM is a single point of failure, and the team must scale and patch the broker itself. Pub/Sub is a managed, scalable service.

sources.title: What is Pub/Sub?
sources.evidence: You can then use a stream processing tool, such as Dataflow, which delivers the events to databases. Examples of such databases are BigQuery, Bigtable, and Cloud Storage. Pub/Sub lets you gather events from many clients simultaneously.

sources.title: Bigtable overview
sources.evidence: Bigtable is ideal for storing large amounts of single-keyed data with low latency. It supports high read and write throughput at low latency, and it's an ideal data source for MapReduce operations.

sources.title: Schema design for time series data
sources.evidence: In this pattern, you create a row for each new event or measurement instead of adding cells to columns in existing rows. The row key suffix is the timestamp value.

stem: KnightMotives's supply chain runs on an outdated mainframe, and few staff understand its code. The outdated ERP depends on this mainframe. The company wants to modernize legacy systems gradually to improve efficiency and agility. Production must not stop during the change. What should you do first?

options.text: Assess the codebase with Mainframe Assessment Tool, and define business domains and migratable units to set priorities.
Rewrite all mainframe applications in Java at the same time, and switch to them in one weekend cutover.
Rehost the mainframe applications on Compute Engine VMs, and assess the codebase after the move is complete.
Copy all mainframe data to BigQuery with Mainframe Connector, and then shut down the mainframe.

explanation: The deciding needs are a gradual change, little knowledge of the code, and no stop in production. Google gives a phased approach and tools for mainframe modernization. Mainframe Assessment Tool uses generative AI to help teams understand the codebase and generate documentation. Domains break the application into smaller, migratable units, so the team can set priorities.

whyWrong.B: A single rewrite and cutover is the opposite of a gradual change. With little knowledge of the code, it puts production at risk.
whyWrong.C: A move before an assessment hides dependencies until they break. The team cannot plan a safe order of moves without first understanding the code.
whyWrong.D: Mainframe Connector moves data, but the mainframe applications still run the supply chain. A shutdown would stop production.

sources.title: Mainframe modernization overview
sources.evidence: Google Cloud provides a phased approach and tools to guide your mainframe modernization journey.

sources.title: Mainframe modernization overview
sources.evidence: define domains when you create an assessment to break down and map your mainframe application into logical business domains and smaller, migratable units to prioritize your migration strategy.

sources.title: Mainframe Assessment Tool overview
sources.evidence: Mainframe Assessment Tool automates assessment, saving you time and resources. It uses generative AI to help you understand your existing codebase and generate documentation.

stem: KnightMotives needs network upgrades to support increased data traffic and improve connectivity between plants and headquarters. Each site will also connect to Google Cloud as part of the hybrid cloud strategy. The network team wants traffic between sites to use Google's network. It does not want to manage a separate link for each pair of sites. What should you recommend?

options.text: Connect each site to its own VPC network, and join all the VPC networks together with VPC Network Peering.
Build a full mesh of IPsec VPN tunnels over the internet between every pair of sites.
Connect each site to Google Cloud with Cross-Cloud Interconnect, and route traffic between sites through those connections.
Attach each site's Cloud Interconnect connection as a spoke of a Network Connectivity Center hub with site-to-site data transfer.

explanation: The deciding needs are site-to-site traffic on Google's network and no link for each pair of sites. With site-to-site data transfer, Network Connectivity Center (NCC) uses Google's network as part of a WAN that includes external sites. Each spoke attaches to a central hub, which gives full mesh connectivity between all spokes. Check that each site is in a supported location.

whyWrong.A: VPC Network Peering connects two VPC networks, and it does not provide transitive routing. It does not make Google's network a WAN between external sites.
whyWrong.B: The number of tunnels grows with each new site, and the team manages every pair. Traffic uses the public internet, not Google's network.
whyWrong.C: Cross-Cloud Interconnect connects Google Cloud to another cloud service provider. It is not a product for plants or headquarters.

sources.title: Site-to-site data transfer overview
sources.evidence: Network Connectivity Center (NCC) lets you use Google's network as part of a wide area network (WAN) that includes your external sites. This feature is known as site-to-site data transfer.

sources.title: Site-to-site data transfer overview
sources.evidence: Then you create a NCC spoke to represent each connectivity resource. Each spoke is attached to a central hub, which provides full mesh connectivity between all of the spokes.

sources.title: NCC overview
sources.evidence: Use a Google Cloud VPC network as an enterprise wide area network (WAN) to connect networks that are outside of Google Cloud. You can establish connectivity between your external sites by using any type of hybrid spoke.

stem: KnightMotives runs some applications on another major cloud platform. These applications now exchange large volumes of data with new workloads on Google Cloud. The team wants dedicated, high-bandwidth connectivity between the two clouds. Traffic must not use the public internet. What should you recommend?

options.text: Cross-Cloud Interconnect between Google Cloud and the other cloud service provider
Dedicated Interconnect from the on-premises data center, with traffic sent through that data center
HA VPN tunnels between Google Cloud and the other cloud over the public internet
Direct Peering between Google's edge network and the other cloud service provider's network

explanation: The deciding needs are a dedicated, high-bandwidth link to another cloud without the public internet. Google recommends Cross-Cloud Interconnect when you connect to another cloud service provider. Google provisions a dedicated physical connection between its network and the network of the other provider.

whyWrong.B: Dedicated Interconnect connects on-premises networks to VPC networks. Cloud-to-cloud traffic through the data center adds hops and uses the data center's links.
whyWrong.C: HA VPN traffic in this option uses the public internet, which the requirement does not allow.
whyWrong.D: Google recommends Cloud Interconnect instead of Direct Peering, which you use only in certain circumstances. For another cloud service provider, Google recommends Cross-Cloud Interconnect.
